name: nutrition-demo
narrative: Priya runs a child-nutrition program funded to deliver RUTF and screen for malnutrition through three network managers — Amara in the Northern Cluster, Bakary in Central, and Chidi in the Eastern. Monday morning she opens the Program Admin Report and reads all three managers' last four weekly reviews as one grid: Northern is meeting the SOP across the board, while Central and Eastern both read below it. She clicks a resolved week in Central's row and an inline panel names the worker who was flagged and links the audit and coaching task that dealt with it. She opens the run behind the cell and reads the same per-worker review Bakary worked from, its buttons now reporting what was done, then opens the flagged worker's audit and sees the child's MUAC photos the auditor passed with her own eyes. She reads the closed coaching conversation and watches that worker's screening numbers recover week over week. Then she turns to the harder cells — Central's still-open investigation, where the coaching is paused mid-exchange, and Eastern's case where the AI image review caught misleading MUAC photos and the worker was suspended. She lands back on the aggregate column and decides for herself which network manager needs her this week. And to see what all that oversight is ultimately for, she opens one flagged child's follow-up timeline and watches the child's MUAC climb visit by visit — from a severe-acute red reading up through yellow into green, recovered — the program-to-child line closing on a child getting better.

priya.name: Priya Sharma
priya.intro: Priya runs a child-nutrition program through three network managers and their frontline teams across the Northern, Central, and Eastern clusters. She needs to know — without reading a dozen separate weekly reviews — which network manager is on top of the MUAC screening SOP and which flagged workers still need attention.

slides.title: The goal — one manager, three programs, every paid visit verified
slides.narration: Connect lets one person oversee several programs at once and act on all of them from a single place — confident that every service being paid for has actually been verified. Here, one manager oversees three network managers running RUTF distribution and weekly MUAC screening. From one screen she checks each manager's SOP compliance, opens a flagged worker's audited photos and the coaching that followed, and tracks an individual child's recovery — every number backed by the verified visit behind it.

slides.title: Priya sees the whole program at a glance
slides.narration: Priya opens the Program Admin Report and sees all three network managers on one grid — four weeks each, with an aggregate that calls out who is meeting the screening SOP. Northern is clean; Central and Eastern both read below.

slides.title: Priya clicks into a resolved week in Central's row
slides.narration: She clicks a resolved week in Central's row. An inline panel names the worker who was flagged — Kadi Fofana — and links straight to the audit and the coaching task that dealt with it, without leaving the report.

slides.title: Priya opens the run behind the cell
slides.narration: She opens the review behind the cell — Bakary's own weekly nutrition review, the per-worker table with its MUAC distribution and SAM and MAM rates, its action buttons now reporting what was already done.

slides.title: Priya checks the child's MUAC photos the auditor saw
slides.narration: She opens the audit and sees the child's MUAC photos herself — each screened child's assessment photo with the auditor's pass-or-fail decision, all on one page.

slides.title: Priya reads the coaching that turned the numbers around
slides.narration: She reads the closed coaching conversation — the full transcript on the task — and watches that worker's screening numbers recover week over week after the manager stepped in.

slides.title: Now the harder case — Central's still-open week
slides.narration: Then the harder cell. Central's still-open week separates a worker whose case is closed from one still under investigation, naming the specific open audit and task.

slides.title: Priya inspects the audit still in review
slides.narration: She opens the in-review audit — MUAC photo cards in mixed states, still reading Save Progress rather than Complete Image Review until every child's photo has a decision.

slides.title: Priya checks on the coaching mid-conversation
slides.narration: The coaching task is still open — its conversation in progress and the Close Task action still available, so the state of an unresolved case is readable straight from the task.

slides.title: The third manager — an AI-caught misleading-photo case
slides.narration: The third manager. Eastern's flagged cell surfaces a worker the AI image review caught submitting misleading MUAC photos — a different fate from a coached-to-close flag or an open case: suspended.

slides.title: Priya opens the audit and sees what the AI flagged
slides.narration: She opens that audit and sees what the AI flagged — the reviewer's own per-photo verdict, a Hyperzoomed badge on the photos where the child's arm isn't visible, so she is verifying the machine's finding against the images, not just a status label.

slides.title: Priya returns to the aggregate and makes her call
slides.narration: She lands back on the aggregate — Northern meeting the SOP, Central and Eastern below, each with runs, flags, and outcomes side by side — the contrast that decides where her week goes.

slides.title: Priya follows one child's recovery
slides.narration: And to see what all that oversight is ultimately for, she follows one child. The SAM follow-up timeline drills to a single child's MUAC climbing across eight visits — out of red, through yellow, into green. Recovered.
